text: First check? It's just six spots.
A check is a note to your bank: pay this person.
Spot one, top right: today's date.
Spot two, pay to the order of: who gets the money.
Spot three: the amount in numbers. Squeeze it right up against the dollar sign,
so this sneaky raccoon can't sneak an extra number in.
Spot four: the same amount, in words. Eight hundred fifty, and zero zero over one hundred.
Then draw a line to the end, so nobody can add more.
Secret: if the words and the numbers don't match, the bank usually trusts the words. So make them match.
Spot five, the memo: what it's for, like your apartment number. It's optional.
Spot six, the big one: sign your name. No signature, no money.
Always use a pen, and never sign a blank check. That's like handing the raccoon your piggy bank.
The numbers at the bottom are your bank's routing number and your account number. Leave them alone.
Six spots, and you just wrote a check. Which spot was new to you?
So next time your landlord says, just write me a check...
